title: Determinism contract (spec acceptance "bake is deterministic") covered only by the manual --verify self-check — no gate pin, no negative leg
evidence:
def verify(out_path: str, cache_dir: str) -> None:
    import tempfile
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".json", delete=False) as tmp:
        tmp_path = tmp.name
    try:
        bake(cache_dir, tmp_path)
        a = open(out_path, "rb").read()
        b = open(tmp_path, "rb").read()
        if a == b:
            print(f"[verify] PASS — re-bake from cache is byte-identical ({len(a)} bytes)")
        else:
            raise SystemExit("[verify] FAIL — re-bake differs! Determinism broken.")
--- tools/lint.sh:87 (the only tool-output pins wired into CI; nothing references osm_extract.py) ---
if ! python3 tools/test_sprite_order.py; then
	echo "FAIL: sprite order pin"
--- tools/test_sprite_order.py:12-13 (the repo convention this check lacks) ---
Includes a negative self-test leg (#79 r2 W4): the comparator must BITE on a
mutated order (repo convention — drift gates prove they bite).
detail: The byte-identity check is committed code that auto-runs on default invocation, but .osm-cache/ is gitignored and no CI/lint gate runs it; verify's FAIL path is never proven to bite — the repo's stated convention for drift gates.
recommended_fix: Add a lint-gate pure-text pin (convention of test_sprite_order.py): parse committed dublin.json, mutate one byte in a copy, prove the comparator FAILS; wire as tools/lint.sh gate.
